_about_en: English for the vision-pass discrepancy fields that quote the patent in Chinese. output/translations.json is the verified index and is applied first, by longest match; it covers the compound names but not the surrounding prose, and substring substitution into free prose produces unreadable half-translated sentences. So each field listed here is hand-authored as a whole sentence, using the verified index's English for every compound name so the wording stays identical to the gold. Keyed by '<page>#<discrepancy index>.<field>' against input/vision/*.json, which is read-only, so these keys are stable. Chinese characters are quoted nowhere: most of these findings are ABOUT the printed characters - a misprint, a homophone, a full-width bracket, a dropped comma - so where the exact characters are the point of the finding, the finding is described in English instead of shown.

marker_labels_en._about_en: The front page numbers its fields with WIPO INID codes rather than with paragraph markers, and two of those field labels are printed in Chinese. English keys for them, so that every marker in page-index.json is addressable in English.

entries.p01#0.drawing_says: The image shows the INID (10) publication-number field carrying its value CN 109678767 A, and the INID (43) publication-date field carrying its value 2019.04.26, as two complete lines in the top-right block, above the first horizontal rule. Both field labels are printed in Chinese and each sits on the same line as its own value. Layout is read from the image, which is authoritative for layout.
entries.p01#0.text_says: The extraction emits the (10) publication-number label as line 3 and the (43) publication-date label as line 4, each with a trailing space and no value after it, then emits 'CN 109678767 A' as line 39 and '2019.04.26' as line 40, after the page-count line. Labels and values have been rejoined here on the authority of the image. A downstream pass that trusts extraction order alone would mis-pair them, and would additionally confuse line 39 with line 41, the left-margin vertical sidebar, which has byte-identical content.
entries.p01#1.drawing_says: The page renders the brackets around the patent agency's firm-type suffix, the six characters meaning 'special general partnership', as wide full-width brackets, and renders the abstract's Chinese commas, semicolons and colon at a compressed advance width that reads as half-width. Verified at high magnification in both places.
entries.p01#1.text_says: The text layer encodes the brackets around that 'special general partnership' suffix as half-width ASCII round brackets, and encodes every prose mark in the abstract as its full-width Chinese form: the comma, the semicolon, the colon, the enumeration mark used for listing, and the small hollow circle that serves as a full stop. Per the born-digital rule the text layer wins for characters, so the Chinese fields carry the encoded forms. Downstream passes must not infer punctuation width from the pixels of this page, and must not carry CN104292137A's genuinely half-width abstract convention across to this patent.
entries.p01#2.text_says: Step 1 lists a catalyst with no identity; step 2 lists base 1 and a catalyst and later base 2; step 3 lists a catalyst. Each is named by the bare generic word alone. The abstract also gives no yield, no temperature, no reaction time and no molar ratio anywhere. All of these must come from the description pages (p03 onward) and none of them has been inferred here.
entries.p02#0.text_says: Claim 3 reads that said catalyst is azobisisobutyronitrile or m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid. Azobisisobutyronitrile is a radical initiator, appropriate to the benzylic bromination of claim 1 step 1); m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid is a peracid oxidant. Both are printed as alternatives for the same slot. Recorded as printed and NOT resolved; a downstream chemistry pass should treat the step-1 catalyst identity as flagged rather than settled.
entries.p02#1.text_says: Claim 1 step 1) charges only solvent, catalyst and hydrobromic acid, the three separated by the Chinese enumeration mark, and then adds hydrogen peroxide dropwise, and claim 2 gives a molar ratio for exactly those four components. Neither the Chinese word for elemental bromine, nor Br2, nor any other bromine reagent is written anywhere on the page. The bromine must come from the hydrobromic acid, presumably oxidised in situ by the hydrogen peroxide, but the page does not say so and this has NOT been written into the transcription.
entries.p02#2.drawing_says: n/a - no drawing on this page. Layout evidence is from the rendered image: the header carries 'CN 109678767 A' at the left, the section title meaning 'Claims' centred with an ideographic space between each of its five characters, and the leaf count reading 1 of 1 at the right, above a full-width horizontal rule; the only mark below the body is a single '2' centred at the foot of the page.
entries.p02#2.text_says: The text layer for this page ends with five items in this order: the spaced section title meaning 'Claims', the leaf count 1 of 1, the page number '2', the publication number 'CN 109678767 A', and the page number '2' a second time. The publication number belongs to the header, not the footer, and the page number '2' appears twice. The same duplication appears at the end of p03's text layer, so it is a systematic artifact of the extraction rather than something printed. Per the rule that the image wins for layout, header and footer above record one publication number and one page number.
entries.p02#3.text_says: The page prints the acid as 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid at all four occurrences, i.e. 3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl, where the strict form is 3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]. This is a bracketing convention only and changes no atom or bond; the printed form is reproduced verbatim in the Chinese field and preserved in the English. Flagged so that a downstream name-to-structure pass does not mis-parse the missing bracket.
entries.p02#4.text_says: Claim 7 opens with the phrase 'in step 2), the said solvent' and prints no comma after the locative character that closes 'in step 2)', where claims 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 all follow that same character with a full-width comma. Reproduced as printed. Otherwise the page is punctuation-consistent: prose commas are full-width U+FF0C, enumeration marks U+3001, semicolons U+FF1B, the single colon U+FF1A, full stops U+3002, ranges U+FF5E, temperature U+2103; while claim numbers, step numbers, locant commas, ratio colons, decimal points and all hyphens are half-width ASCII. No space character occurs anywhere in the 37 body lines.
entries.p03#0.text_says: Paragraph [0002] prints that the activity of the target is higher than that of mesotrione, using a three-character Chinese head term for mesotrione and glossing it in brackets with two longer Chinese synonyms, one of four characters and one of five. Paragraph [0003] uses the four-character synonym twice as its own head term. The four-character and five-character forms are both standard Chinese names for mesotrione; the three-character head term of [0002] is not standard. Both forms come from the embedded text layer and were confirmed in the ink at high magnification. Recorded as printed, not harmonised.
entries.p03#1.text_says: Paragraph [0006] runs the clause 'a process for synthesising tembotrione from that starting material' straight into 'when preparing methyl 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl...', with no comma after the word for process, whereas [0005] and [0007] both place a full-width comma at exactly that point in the same construction. Confirmed in both the text layer and the ink. Almost certainly a dropped comma, transcribed verbatim and left unfixed; the English keeps the joined construction.
entries.p03#2.drawing_says: The image shows, in reading order: running head 'CN 109678767 A' at the left, the section title meaning 'Description' centred with an ideographic space between each of its three characters, and the leaf count 1 of 9 at the right, under a full-width rule; then the title; then the body; then a single centred '3' at the foot. Nothing else is on the page.
entries.p03#2.text_says: The text layer ends with this sequence: the spaced section title meaning 'Description', the leaf count 1 of 9, the page number '3', the publication number 'CN 109678767 A', and the page number '3' a second time - the head and footer components appended after the body, and '3' appearing twice where the ink shows it once. Layout was taken from the image per the run's rule that the image wins for layout and the text layer wins for characters; the duplicate '3' is treated as an extraction artifact and the footer is recorded once.
entries.p03#3.text_says: Paragraph [0007] prints the enol-ester intermediate, 3-oxo-1-cyclohexen-1-yl 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate, WITH a hyphen joining the acid half of the Chinese ester name to the 3-oxo locant of the alcohol half, while the patent it is describing, CN104292137A, prints the same name without that hyphen. Same compound; the hyphen is orthographic and is not a locant on the benzoic acid ring.
entries.p04#0.text_says: Paragraph [0018] reads: charge to the reaction flask, heat to reflux and react, and when the reaction is complete strip off the solvent entirely; then charge cyclohexane-1,3-dione and solvent to the reaction flask and add triethylamine dropwise below 30 C. The acid chloride is formed and the solvent stripped in flask one; cyclohexane-1,3-dione, solvent and triethylamine are charged to flask two; no sentence joins them. The transfer is inferable from the fact that a single product is obtained, but it is NOT written, and it has not been inferred into the transcription or the translation.
entries.p04#1.text_says: Paragraph [0020] reads 'said catalyst is azobisisobutyronitrile or m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid'. Verified in the image character by character: the second reagent carries the meta prefix character and reads m-chloroperoxybenzoic acid, distinct both from the perbenzoic acid printed in CN104292137A, whose Chinese name is the same string without that meta character, and from benzoyl peroxide, whose Chinese name differs again in two characters. Paragraph [0019] loads it at 0.01-0.1 equivalents, i.e. as an initiator. Recorded as printed; a downstream chemistry pass should treat the initiator identity as flagged rather than settled.
entries.p04#2.text_says: Paragraph [0016] charges a solvent and [0018] charges a catalyst plus two solvents, each named by the bare generic word alone, but the definition paragraphs on this page stop at [0023], which covers only step 2)'s bases and catalyst. Paragraph [0021] defines solvents for step 1) alone. This is almost certainly continuation on the following page rather than an omission, but it is recorded so a pass reading p04 in isolation does not treat the route as fully specified.
entries.p04#3.text_says: Paragraph [0021] encodes the step-1 solvent list, dichloromethane, 1,2-dichloroethane or chloroform, with a literal U+0020 space between the '1' and the comma of the 1,2- locant. The image shows CNIPA justification air on both sides of that comma, so the printed token reads '1 , 2-'. Reproduced verbatim in the Chinese field per the no-normalisation rule; the compound is 1,2-dichloroethane. It is the only embedded space inside a locant string on this page, and every other locant run ('2,2,2-', '1,3-') is unspaced.
entries.p04#4.text_says: The text layer emits, after the body, this sequence: the spaced section title meaning 'Description', the leaf count 2 of 9, the page number '4', the publication number 'CN 109678767 A', and the page number '4' a second time. The image shows exactly one '4', centred at the foot of the page, and the header band with 'CN 109678767 A' at the left, the 'Description' title centred and the leaf count 2 of 9 at the right. The second '4' has no visible counterpart on the page and is treated as a duplicated PDF text object, not as page content. The image was taken as authoritative for layout here, per the layout-vs-characters rule.
entries.p04#5.what: Text-vs-text. One character in the prior-art criticism is printed as the character meaning 'again' where the sentence requires its homophone, the character meaning 'during' or 'in the course of'. The two are written differently and pronounced alike.
entries.p04#5.text_says: Paragraph [0009] reads 'because it is extremely volatile, it readily causes chronic poisoning accidents again the production process', where the sense demanded is 'during the production process'. Verified in the image at high magnification as the 'again' character, not the 'during' character. Almost certainly a typing error for the homophone. Transcribed and translated as printed per the no-typo-fixing rule; it carries no chemical content.
entries.p05#0.drawing_says: Reaction row 4 (page y 1389-1712) shows cyclohexane-1,3-dione plus the benzoyl chloride reacting to the final triketone. Reaction row 5, printed BELOW it at page y 1739-2040, shows the benzoic acid plus thionyl chloride giving that same benzoyl chloride. Row 5 therefore produces row 4's starting material.
entries.p05#1.drawing_says: No DMF and no catalyst label appears at any position in any of the five reaction rows. Row 5, where the acid chloride is formed, carries an entirely bare arrow.
entries.p05#1.text_says: Paragraph [0025] gives a catalyst at 0.01-0.1 equivalents in step 3) and [0027] identifies it as DMF. A reagent written but not drawn.
entries.p05#4.drawing_says: Row 1 uses HBr plus H2O2 with a catalyst labelled 'cat'. Row 2 uses HOCH2CF3 plus an unspecified base, written on the arrow as the single Chinese character for base. Row 3 is labelled with that same base character over the single character for acid, meaning base then acid.
entries.p05#4.text_says: None of HBr, H2O2, the 'cat' label, HOCH2CF3, the bare base character or the base-over-acid label appears anywhere in [0024] to [0029]. They are drawn but not written on this page. The prose for those steps is on earlier pages and was not available to this pass, so this is flagged as unverified rather than as a conflict.
entries.p05#5.drawing_says: Row 4's arrow label reads triethylamine over acetone cyanohydrin and row 5's co-reactant reads thionyl chloride, all three named in Chinese on the scheme. Row 4's left-hand structure is drawn as cyclohexane-1,3-dione (two C=O separated by one CH2).
entries.p05#5.text_says: Paragraph [0025] names thionyl chloride, cyclohexane-1,3-dione, triethylamine and acetone cyanohydrin. Drawing and prose agree on all four, including the 1,3 substitution pattern of the dione, which is read off the drawing independently.
entries.p05#6.drawing_says: The printed page shows no spaces inside the bracketed (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy) group of the name in [0025], and it does show a small Chinese full stop, the hollow circle mark, at page x 317-323, y 2082-2088 below the last reaction row.
entries.p05#6.text_says: The text layer encodes that bracketed (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy) group with a space before each of its locant commas, while encoding the name of cyclohexane-1,3-dione in the same sentence with no such space, and it contains no character at all for the small Chinese full stop, which is part of the scheme graphic. The Chinese fields keep the text layer verbatim per the instruction for this born-digital document; both facts are recorded so a later reader can tell which is which.
entries.p06#2.text_says: Paragraph [0035] reads 'the following gives a further detailed description of this aspect in conjunction with the examples, but this description shall not constitute a limitation of this aspect'. The three characters rendered here as 'this aspect' are what the embedded text layer contains, so this is not a reading error on this pass; compare [0030] on the same page, which uses the normal three-character phrase for 'the present invention'. The two phrases share their first character and differ in the second and third. Transcribed and translated verbatim; not corrected.
entries.p06#3.text_says: Paragraph [0040] says only 200 ml of dichloroethane, the Chinese name carrying no locant, and never 1,2-dichloroethane. 1,2-dichloroethane is the solvent this would conventionally be, but the isomer is not stated anywhere on the page and has NOT been inferred into the transcription or the translation.
entries.p06#4.text_says: Paragraphs [0033] and [0037] both name the target with a three-character Chinese common name for tembotrione. The sister publication CN104292137A uses a four-character form: the same three characters with one more inserted before the last. Both denote tembotrione. The form on this page is verified from the embedded text layer, so the shorter spelling is what this document actually prints.
entries.p06#5.drawing_says: The rendered page image shows exactly one footer, the page number '6' centred at the bottom, and one header line: 'CN 109678767 A' at the left, the spaced section title meaning 'Description' centred, and the leaf count 4 of 9 at the right.
entries.p06#5.text_says: The extracted text layer emits the header and footer OUT OF READING ORDER, after the body text, and emits the page number '6' TWICE: the tail of the file reads the spaced section title meaning 'Description', then the leaf count 4 of 9, then '6', then 'CN 109678767 A', then '6' again. The image wins on layout per instruction: there is one footer '6', not two. The duplicate is a PDF text-object artifact.
entries.p07#0.text_says: The raw text layer line reads, in Chinese, 'take 27 .4g 2-chloro-3-(2 ,2 ,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid (99 .7%,' - a space before the decimal point of 27.4, a space before each locant comma inside the trifluoroethoxy bracket, and a space before the decimal point of the purity figure. Re-read at high magnification the page prints 27.4g, the (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy) bracket and (99.7% with no internal spaces, and the same tokens are emitted unspaced elsewhere in the same file (line 21 gives 99.7% cleanly), so the spaces are an extraction artifact of CNIPA's fixed-width digit cells. They were removed in the Chinese field for [0046] and nowhere else. This is the only place any Chinese field on this page departs from the text layer byte for byte.
entries.p07#1.text_says: Paragraph [0046] names thionyl chloride, DMF, cyclohexane-1,3-dione, triethylamine and acetone cyanohydrin, and [0051] names azobisisobutyronitrile, hydrobromic acid and hydrogen peroxide. None of these is drawn. This is the patent's convention of captioning each numbered step with its product alone, not damage or an omission, but a downstream pass must not read these drawings as schemes: the transformations exist only in the prose.
entries.p07#2.text_says: Paragraph [0046] goes from the acid plus thionyl chloride straight to adding cyclohexane-1,3-dione and triethylamine, then adds acetone cyanohydrin, then works up to the product. The acid chloride and the enol ester that acetone cyanohydrin rearranges are implied by the reagent order but are named nowhere and drawn nowhere. They have NOT been inferred into any field.
entries.p07#3.text_says: Paragraph [0046] says only dichloroethane, twice, the Chinese name carrying no locant in either place, and never 1,2-dichloroethane. The 1,2-isomer is the usual reading but the isomer is not stated on the page and has not been supplied in the transcription or the translation.
entries.p07#4.text_says: CNIPA's fixed-width setting renders the half-width round brackets as visually wide glyphs and compresses the full-width comma toward a Western comma, so the two cannot be told apart by eye on the rendered page. Per the born-digital rule the text layer is authoritative for characters: parentheses on this page are half-width; prose commas are the full-width form U+FF0C; enumeration marks are U+3001; and the percent signs (U+FF05), tilde ranges (U+FF5E) and the degree-Celsius sign (U+2103) are full-width. The header uses the ideographic space U+3000 between the three characters of the section title meaning 'Description'.
entries.p08#1.text_says: Paragraphs [0055] and [0059] name the product only by its three-character Chinese common name, tembotrione, which fixes the constitution but says nothing about tautomer. Not a conflict, but recorded so a downstream pass generating a canonical structure does not assume the enol form from the name or assume the keto form from the drawing.
entries.p08#2.text_says: Paragraphs [0055] and [0059] both write the three-character Chinese name for tembotrione. The usual CNIPA form has four characters: the same three with one more inserted before the last. Both denote tembotrione. Recorded as printed and not corrected.
entries.p08#3.text_says: Paragraph [0057] prints the substituent as '3- (2 ,2 ,2-trifluoroethoxy)' and the purity as '(99 .8%', with spaces inside the locant string and inside the number; [0063] prints the same fragment tight as (2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy), and [0054] prints 99.8% tight. Reproduced verbatim in every case. This is CNIPA justification whitespace and carries no chemical meaning.
entries.p08#4.text_says: Paragraph [0054] reads, literally, 'into the residue 4.53 g sodium hydroxide (99%, 0.112 mol), 200 ml water, carry out alkaline hydrolysis at 70 to 75 C'. The Chinese construction opens with 'into the residue' and requires a governing verb meaning 'add', and that verb is absent from the publication. The English brackets the missing verb; the Chinese is left exactly as extracted.
entries.p09#0.text_says: Text layer, carrying the spaces the extractor inserted: 'take 34 .75g', the bracketed '(2 ,2 ,2-trifluoroethoxy)' group, '(99 .7%', 'take 11 .3g', and 'cyclohexane-1 ,3-dione'. Rendered image, verified at 2x magnification: 'take 34.75g', '(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)', '(99.7%', 'take 11.3g', and 'cyclohexane-1,3-dione'. The Chinese field reproduces the text layer verbatim as instructed; the correct printed values are 34.75 g, 99.7 %, 11.3 g and the 2,2,2- and 1,3- locants. No other paragraph on the page is affected.
entries.p09#1.text_says: Paragraph [0065] ends 'dried to give 31.58 g of a white powder, purity 99.3%, yield 90.5%' - 31.58 g of a white powder, with no compound name. Paragraph [0068] then charges 2-chloro-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid as its starting material, which is the same compound as the drawing. The three agree, but the naming link is implicit.
entries.p09#2.text_says: Paragraph [0068] says only dichloroethane in both places it appears, the Chinese name carrying no locant either time, and never 1,2-dichloroethane. The 1,2-isomer is the conventional reading but is nowhere stated on this page, and has not been inferred into the transcription or the translation.
entries.p09#3.text_says: Paragraph [0071] titles the step 'Synthesis of methyl 2-chloro-3-bromomethyl-4-methylsulfonylbenzoate', its leading item number '1' separated from the name by the Chinese enumeration mark, i.e. the synthesis of the bromomethyl ester. Paragraph [0073] then begins 'take 26.43 g of methyl 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-(methylsulfonyl)benzoate' - the 3-METHYL ester, the substrate. Same convention holds for the drawing at [0064] relative to [0065]: every drawing on this page is a step product, and no drawing on this page is a reaction scheme.
entries.p09#4.text_says: The sentence reads, literally, 'into the residue 4.04 g sodium hydroxide (99%, 0.1 mol), 200 ml water, carry out alkaline hydrolysis at 70 to 75 C'. It carries no verb meaning 'add', nor any equivalent, between the opening phrase 'into the residue' and the reagent list. Transcribed as printed; the English supplies the verb in square brackets so the gap stays visible.
entries.p09#5.text_says: The embedded text layer holds half-width ASCII round brackets everywhere on this page. The printed glyphs are visually wide, occupying a full ideographic em, as CNIPA typesetting renders them. The text layer is taken as authoritative for the character per the extraction rule, so the Chinese fields carry ASCII parentheses. The full-width percent sign (U+FF05), comma (U+FF0C), enumeration mark (U+3001), full stop (U+3002), colon (U+FF1A), tilde range mark (U+FF5E) and degree-Celsius sign (U+2103) are all genuinely full-width in the text layer and are reproduced as such.
entries.p10#0.text_says: Paragraph [0076] prints '2.26g triethylenediamine (99%, 0.01mol)'. Triethylenediamine (DABCO) MW 112.17, so 0.01 mol at 99% purity is 1.13 g, not 2.26 g; 2.26 g corresponds to 0.02 mol. Transcribed exactly as printed and NOT corrected. Downstream mass-balance passes must treat the mass and the mole figure for this reagent as mutually inconsistent and pick one deliberately rather than silently.
entries.p10#1.text_says: Paragraph [0076] prints '1.13g2,2,2-trifluoroethanol (99%, 0.2mol)', with no space between the mass and the name. 2,2,2-Trifluoroethanol MW 100.04, so 0.2 mol at 99% purity is 20.2 g, not 1.13 g; 1.13 g corresponds to about 0.011 mol, i.e. only 0.11 equivalent against the 0.1 mol of benzylic bromide, which cannot support the printed 89.3% yield. Recorded as a factual observation and NOT acted on: the value 1.13 g is exactly the mass that 0.01 mol of triethylenediamine at 99% would require, and 2.26 g in the preceding clause is exactly 0.02 mol of triethylenediamine, so the two masses look transposed or otherwise garbled at typesetting. No substitution has been made in the transcription; the printed characters stand.
entries.p10#2.drawing_says: The rendered page (each token inspected on a crop enlarged 2x to 3x) prints, without any gap: 30.66g / 1.13g / 31.1g / 34.72g / (99.8% / 0.1mol / 0.74g / 0.01mol / 0.2mol / 22.6g / (2,2,2- / 1,3-
entries.p10#2.text_says: The embedded text layer emits: '30 .66g' / '1 .13g' / '31 .1g' / '34 .72g' / '(99 .8%' / '0 .1mol' / '0 .74g' / '0 .01mol' / '0 .2mol' / '22 .6g' / '(2 ,2 ,2-' / '1 ,3-'. These are kerning artifacts of the extractor. The image governs layout, so the spurious spaces were removed in the Chinese fields; both forms are recorded here so the decision is fully reversible. No digit, decimal point or comma was added, dropped or changed.
entries.p10#3.drawing_says: The rendered page shows the header as three separated fields on one ruled line ('CN 109678767 A' at the left, the section title meaning 'Description' centred with an ideographic space between each of its three characters, and the leaf count 8 of 9 at the right) and a single centred footer '10' at the very bottom, with nothing else below the last body line.
entries.p10#3.text_says: The text layer ends with this sequence: the spaced section title meaning 'Description', the leaf count 8 of 9, the page number '10', the publication number 'CN 109678767 A', and the page number '10' a second time, i.e. the page number 10 appears twice and the publication number follows rather than precedes the centred title. The image ordering was used for the header and footer fields; the duplicate is an extraction artifact and carries no page content.
entries.p10#4.text_says: Paragraph [0076] reads, literally, 'into the residue 8.1 g sodium hydroxide (99%, 0.2 mol), 200 ml water, carry out alkaline hydrolysis at 70 to 75 C'. The Chinese frame that brackets 'the residue' between a preposition and a locative particle has no governing verb: no word meaning 'add' or its equivalent appears. Transcribed as printed and translated with the same ellipsis rather than supplying the missing verb.
entries.p10#6.text_says: Paragraph [0077] names the target with the three-character Chinese common name for tembotrione. The reference patent CN104292137A names the same target with a four-character form: the same three characters with one more inserted before the last. Both denote tembotrione. Transcribed as printed here; no normalisation applied.
entries.p11#0.text_says: The heading meaning 'Comparative Example' is printed as [0080] on PAGE 10, one page earlier, and the step-1 heading as [0081]. Neither is repeated on this page. Paragraph [0090] on this page confirms the attribution from the other direction: it names elemental bromine, acetonitrile and sodium methoxide as the hazardous reagents the invention avoids, and those are exactly the reagents used by [0083], [0089] and [0086] here.
entries.p11#1.text_says: Paragraph [0083] gives only elemental bromine (Br2), carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) and an instruction to heat to reflux. No AIBN, no benzoyl peroxide, no peroxide of any kind and no irradiation is mentioned. The invention's own corresponding step [0073] on page 10 does use AIBN. Recorded as printed; no initiator has been inferred into the transcription.
entries.p11#2.what: Printed typo carried through verbatim: the two-character verb meaning 'distil off' is printed with its first character replaced by a different character, the one meaning 'to arrange' or 'to put in order'.
entries.p11#2.text_says: Paragraph [0089] reads 'then [arrange] off the solvent and the excess thionyl chloride'. The character printed there, zheng, means 'to arrange' and makes no sense governing the word for solvent; the verb plainly intended is the two-character compound meaning 'distil off', which differs from what is printed only in that first character. The very same paragraph set uses the correct verb twice in [0086], distilling off DMF and distilling off ethanol. Both the embedded text layer and the rendered image agree on the wrong character, so this is the publication's own error, not an extraction fault. Transcribed verbatim and translated with the misprint marked in place.
entries.p11#3.what: Printed word-order error carried through verbatim: the locative particle meaning 'in' or 'inside' is misplaced in the solvent phrase, standing between the volume and the solvent name instead of after the solvent name.
entries.p11#3.text_says: Paragraph [0089] reads, literally, 'dissolved in 200 ml in dichloromethane', with the locative particle sitting between the volume and the solvent name. The standard order puts that particle last, after the solvent name, giving 'dissolved in 200 ml of dichloromethane'. The meaning is not in doubt - 200 ml of dichloromethane - but the characters are reproduced as printed.
entries.p11#4.text_says: Paragraph [0086] reads 'adjusted to acidic with HCL', with a capital L. Elsewhere the description writes hydrochloric acid out as a Chinese word ([0089]) rather than as a formula, so there is no competing spelling on this page. Reproduced as printed.
entries.p11#5.text_says: Paragraph [0086] ends 'a yellow solid precipitated, the yield was 83.2%', the percent sign printed in its full-width form. No product name, no product mass, no substrate quantity and no trifluoroethanol quantity are given anywhere in the paragraph, so the 83.2% cannot be checked against anything. The heading [0084] does name the acid, which agrees with the drawing.
entries.p11#7.text_says: Paragraph [0089] reads '4 drops of acetone cyanohydrin', the quantity given as a drop count and nothing else. Every other reagent in that paragraph carries both a mass and a molar figure. A downstream mass-balance pass must treat this loading as unquantified rather than estimating a drop volume.
entries.p11#8.text_says: Volume units are printed 'mL' in [0083] and [0086] but 'ml' in [0089]. Paragraph [0089] prints the pH as 'PH' followed by a full-width equals sign and '2', with an upper-case P and an upper-case H rather than 'pH'. This patent writes the target with the three-character Chinese name for tembotrione throughout, whereas the reference patent CN104292137A writes a four-character form of the same name for the same compound. Paragraph [0090] shortens the five-character heading meaning 'Comparative Example', as headed at [0080] on page 10, to a three-character abbreviation that drops its two middle characters. All reproduced as printed.
